title: Buying property, the 1929 crash and returning to Parks
summary: He bought three properties in New Orleans, survived the Depression with his father-in-law's loan and developed land in Parks.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Dancing and everything else, you know what I mean. You see how second line followed? That's the way they did. And so when I'd get home I'd tell my wife, I'd say, the sooner I can give this thing up, I'd say the better. I'd say, because I want to play just for me and you if I can do what I want to do. Because I was buying property, you see. I was investing the little nickels that I was making. And I'd say as soon as I could get enough of it I was going to retire. But before I retired, well then I got sick. Where did you buy? I had done bought three pieces of property. One of them wasn't paid for but I had done paid for them. This was property in New Orleans? New Orleans. I had two pieces on two row and one on Gallagher's. I was doing well. But that crash, you see, that 1929 and 1930, we had a soup line from here to the church over there. Everywhere you could turn around and people crying. So many people losing their property.
That's right. You'd have 100 people in line, 200 or 300?
Oh, easily 100. More than that too.
Those were the days out here right now.

Bank all closed. Tried to borrow money to save this place here. I couldn't borrow it. My father-in-law was the one that caused I to get this place. Because he had the money and he loaned me the money. So I saved this place. That was my father's place right here. And my father had a heavy mortgage on the place and I had to pay that mortgage off to it so I could acquire the property. So I did it. And now today I'm glad I did it because New Orleans got so close on me until I couldn't get around and I was glad to come here. Yes, indeed. And I wish I'd have been here a long time before that. I wish I didn't play some of them in the parade and see them doing it right here. Because I could have made good here. Sure, because when I came here I was doing wonderfully well. It's just a question of being by myself, you see, everybody else could help me. So I just went down. But then I think I did wonderfully well at that because I was selling lots back there and I got some more land back there. I was renting to the people for the crop. And I sold the school, I gave the school, I sold the church, I gave the church, and improving the community all the time. I think it's going along nicely. And I got three or four home families back there.
You gave the land for the church or what?
Not give, the whole thing, give them a part. Give them a part. Yeah, because I wanted to see the community. Yes, it's going along.
It's a nice church. I just lived there. It's a nice church.
